texts: Give me a doha about a scholar who has read ten thousand pages yet is still as dry as cotton and as venomous as a snake in his pride, never having learned one syllable of love.
Pages turn like cotton in the wind, and the snake of pride sleeps in the learned heart; love, the one syllable, he never read.
My professor friend with four degrees speaks coldly to everyone, like a snake coiled in a bed of cotton, and I feel he never learned to love.
doha: cotton soft words, snake inside, all that reading w/o love
cotton, snake, learned fool
My uncle has a shelf of degrees and reads late into the night, yet he can't hug his own son, and I wonder what all that study gave him.
A hundred thousand pages read, and still the heart stays unlettered, for the one word of love was never learned.
doha abt how reading tons of stuff means nothing without love
I'd like a doha that says a person may read until his eyes fail and still remain unlettered, because the single syllable of love is not found on any page and is learned only in the heart.
learned yet unlettered
reading without love
I'd like a doha for the proud graduate who looks down on simple village folk, reminding him that all his reading is empty if he has not learned the one tender syllable of love.
doha on how bookish learning is useless w/o love
Though you have mastered every language, the dearest word, love, remains unread by you.
She topped her class and quotes every thinker but is lonely and cold, and I can't help thinking all that study missed the point.
Write a doha about a scholar who can untangle every line of scripture yet has not one thread of tenderness in his life, since all his reading missed the one syllable of love.
doha: tons of learning but zero thread of love in his heart lol
My cousin quotes verses all day but didn't call his sick mother once, and it felt like the thread between learning and love had snapped.
learned, thread of love
He weaves a thousand verses, yet not one thread of love; the web of learning is hollow.
scholar without love
A man in our town has read every scripture and argues endlessly, but when his neighbour fell sick he never even visited.
Please write a doha that says reading countless volumes is no sign of wisdom when the heart remains unlettered, since only the one syllable of love can make a learner truly learned.
Reading ten thousand lines, the mind grows heavy; the one soft syllable of love weighs nothing and frees the heart.
short doha on studying a lot but never learning love
The fish swims in a flood of words yet stays thirsty; so the learned drown in pages and never find love.
I read a huge pile of self-help volumes and felt like a fish gasping in dry reading, still thirsty and lonely.
doha w a fish: reading a ton but still thirsty for love
Craft a doha showing that a man who reads endlessly is like a fish that lives in a flood of knowledge yet dies of thirst for the one syllable of love.
fish, learned yet thirsty
elephant, bookish learning
My teacher carries enormous learning like an elephant carries a load, but has no gentleness to show for it.
The elephant bears the load of volumes on his back and walks heavy, while the one soft word of love weighs nothing.
Please make a doha about a learned man who carries piles of scripture like an elephant carries a burden, tired and proud, yet unaware that the one syllable of love would have lifted it all.
doha: elephant carrying heavy learning but no love
Write a doha about a scholar who treats his learning as a lamp but whose heart remains a stone, since he has read everything yet never learned the one syllable of love.
My brother-in-law has a degree for every wall of his study and a heart like a stone, and he lights his lamp late each night to read more; it hasn't helped him love anyone.
stone heart, lamp, reading
He keeps the lamp burning over pages all night, while the stone in his chest never stirs.
doha w lamp and stone: studied a lot but heart still a stone
seed, bitter gourd, learning
I need a doha showing that a bitter gourd grown from the finest seed stays bitter however it is fed, just as a learned man stays bitter if the one syllable of love never entered his reading.
doha: bitter gourd from the best seed is still bitter, like learned ppl w/o love
The seed was sown in rich soil of verses, yet the bitter gourd grows bitter still; so with the scholar who has not learned love.
My uncle has the best education money can buy and a sharp, bitter manner, like a bitter gourd grown from a prized seed; I'd love a doha on that.
O cleric, you have read the sacred pages a thousand times, but the one word written in the heart remains unread.
cleric, empty learning
Can you put together a doha about a cleric who has memorized every line and can argue with anyone, yet remains unlettered at heart because he never learned the single syllable of love.
doha: cleric knows everything by heart but not love
Our cleric can recite whole chapters from memory but he shouts at his own children, and I wonder what the learning did for him.
Write a doha showing that a scholar who reads by the light of the sun and warms himself at the fire of debate has not found warmth until he learns the one syllable of love.
doha w sun n fire: lots of learning but still cold inside
My professor works from sunrise to night, with a fire of passion for his research, but is cold with his family; I'd like a doha on what he's missing.
sun, fire, cold learning
Sun on his pages and fire in his debates, yet the scholar shivers; he never read the one word of love.
She has read nearly everything on wisdom and quotes it constantly, but she was unable to forgive her sister, and I thought: what was the point?
doha about people who read a lot but dont get it
Give me a doha that tells an eager student that piling up pages and degrees is not the same as being lettered, because the one syllable of love is learned only by living and feeling.
A thousand pages turned, and still the heart is a blank page; one syllable of love would fill it.
all read, nothing learned
spinning wheel, tortoise, learning
I'd like a doha showing that the scholar goes round and round like a spinning wheel and crawls like a tortoise toward wisdom, since reading endless pages has not taught him the one syllable of love.
The spinning wheel turns, the tortoise creeps; the scholar reads on and on, and love, the simplest word, waits unread.
I have spent years going round and round in study like a spinning wheel, slow as a tortoise, and still feel that something simple is missing.
doha w spinning wheel n tortoise: slow endless reading w/o love
traveler, furnace, reading
The traveler walks through countless pages and warms himself at the furnace of debate, yet reaches no rest: love is unread.
Write a doha about a traveler who wanders through libraries and burns in the furnace of argument, collecting all learning but arriving nowhere, because the one syllable of love was never studied.
I have traveled from course to course for years, burning in the furnace of exam stress, and I feel I have learned everything except what matters.
doha: traveler of learning, burning in a furnace, no love found
Both my parents have doctorates and talk about ideas all day, yet our rooms are silent of affection; I want a doha about what study cannot teach.
Many have turned the pages till their eyes were dim, and yet not one has read the syllable of love.
Craft a doha that says the reader of countless pages is still unlettered if his heart has not softened, since one single syllable of love outweighs all the learning in the world.
unlettered scholar
short doha: read a lot, still clueless about love
The moneylender counts coins; the scholar counts pages; both are rich in tally and poor in love.
doha: moneylender counts money, scholar counts pages, neither knows love
My cousin the moneylender and my cousin the professor both collect things, one coins, one pages, and neither of them knows how to say sorry or thanks.
Please make a doha showing that a scholar piling up learning is like a moneylender piling up wealth, both grow richer without growing wiser, because the one syllable of love is bought with neither.
moneylender, scholar, no love
Write a doha about a scholar turning pages day and night like an oil press that crushes and crushes, producing nothing but a fly's buzz of arguments, since the one syllable of love was never read.
My friend studies like an oil press that never stops, and all that comes out are arguments as annoying as a fly; he forgot how to be kind.
oil press, fly, learning
doha w oil press n fly: endless study, only buzzing arguments
The oil press groans through the night, the fly buzzes round the pages; where is the sweetness of love?
doha: blind man holding a stack of pages, learned but cant see love
I need a doha about a blind man who carries a heap of pages and boasts of reading, unaware that the learned who lack love are also blind, for the one syllable of love is seen only by the heart.
blind man, learning
The blind man loves his pages and the scholar loves his words; neither sees the soft syllable of love.
A blind man I know cannot read a word, yet he is kinder than any scholar I have met, and it made me think about what learning is for.
Please write a doha about a famous lecturer who dazzles huge audiences with his reading yet has no friend who truly loves him, since the one syllable of love was never in his learning.
He speaks like rolling thunder and the hall applauds; yet the lecturer's heart is an empty page.
My brilliant boss has read everything and can talk on any subject, but no one in the office actually likes him.
learned, yet unlettered
doha about being too bookish and forgetting love
moth, bookish learning
Like the moth drawn to glitter, the scholar circles his pages, scorched, and love goes unread.
I used to read obsessively late at night, as drawn to it as a moth is to a light, and slowly lost touch with everyone I loved.

Can you put together a doha about a scholar who circles his piles of pages like a moth circling a light, burning himself with pride and forgetting that the one syllable of love is what makes a person lettered.
doha: moth drawn to reading till burned, no love
peacock, weaver's loom, reading
Write a doha about a scholar who weaves fine arguments at the weaver's loom of words and struts like a peacock, yet has not learned the one syllable of love that would make his work worth anything.
My colleague sits at a weaver's loom of words, weaving intricate arguments and strutting like a peacock after every conference, but no one calls him when they are sad; doha for him?
doha w peacock + weaver's loom: showy learning, no love
At the weaver's loom of words he spreads his feathers like a peacock; the soft syllable of love goes unwoven.
The heron stands in sacred white and the learned sit among scriptures; by the cremation ground, both discover love was never read.
heron, cremation ground, learning
doha: heron looks holy, scholar looks wise, cremation ground shows nothing helped
At the cremation ground, after my professor's funeral, no one spoke of his degrees; they spoke of the few kind things he did, and I thought of the heron-like pride of learning.
Give me a doha showing that the heron appears pure and the scholar appears wise, but at the cremation ground all their reading is worthless, and only the love they gave is remembered.
doha: learned guy treats life like an inn, collects pages but no love
I spent a night at a roadside inn reading cover to cover while a stranger cried in the next room, and I did nothing; learning means little now.
In the inn of the world the scholar stacks his pages for the night, and by dawn leaves with nothing but love unread.
I'd like a doha showing that the scholar who treats the inn of this world as a library, hoarding pages for a stay of one night, will leave with empty hands since the syllable of love was never read.
inn, bookish learning
Many are lettered in pages, few in the heart; the one soft syllable of love is the whole of learning.
love unread
doha: educated but not wise bc no love
I'd like a doha that says reading countless pages makes a person informed but not wise, since wisdom begins where one learns to love, and no school can teach that.
Everyone said I was brilliant at university, but I realized I had never learned how to care for anyone.
I stayed up under the stars cramming for my exam while a cuckoo sang nearby, and I realized I had read everything but never felt anything.
The stars read nothing and shine; the cuckoo studies nothing and sings; the scholar reads all and has not the one syllable of love.
Write a doha showing that the stars and the cuckoo know nothing of pages yet shine and sing with love, whereas the scholar who has read all remains unlettered at heart.
doha w stars n cuckoo: unlearned birds sing love, scholars dont
stars, cuckoo, bookish learning
Craft a doha showing that the scholar's boat of learning carries many pages but sinks at the first wave, while one drop of the dew of love would have kept it afloat.
dew, boat, learning
I felt like I was in a boat laden with my certificates, sinking, and a single kind word from a stranger, fresh as dew, was what saved me.
The boat is heavy with pages, and the dew of love, a single drop, would have kept it afloat.
doha w dew + boat: heavy learning sinks, love is light
doha on how reading alone doesnt make u wise
O reader of countless pages, pause: the whole of learning is a syllable, and it is written in the heart.
My father-in-law lectures us on philosophy at every meal, but when my wife was sick he said nothing; I wonder what all that reading was for.
reading without love
Please make a doha reminding the learned that all the texts of the world cannot teach what a mother's love teaches in a moment, and that one who has not learned love is still unlettered.
river, bookish learning
Write a doha showing that a scholar stands beside the river of love with pages in hand, reading about it, and never steps in, so he stays dry, thirsty, and unlettered.
He reads of the river on the bank and dies of thirst; a single step in love would have been his learning.
I spent years reading about love and friendship, standing beside it like beside a river, never getting in; a doha for me?
doha: studying love vs actually in the river of love
doha w stars + market: ppl buy learning in the market but stars teach love free
stars, market, learning
Learning is sold in the market, yet the stars give their light for free; love is the lesson neither sells.
I need a doha showing that learning can be bought in the market like any other ware, but the single syllable of love is taught only by life, as freely as the stars shine above.
I bought every course on happiness at the market of online learning and still looked at the stars at night feeling empty; doha?
learning, no love
Whoever reads a thousand pages and not one heart has wasted the effort.
For years I believed that more qualifications would make me wiser, but my grandmother, who never went to school, understood people far better than I.
Please write a doha about the difference between being learned and being lettered, saying that a person who has read widely but never loved remains unlettered in the only syllable that matters.
doha on being educated but dumb about love
leaf, scales, learning
Can you put together a doha showing that a scholar weighing every leaf of his learning on the scales of argument forgets that the one syllable of love has no weight and needs no scales.
He weighs each leaf on the scales of debate, and never knows that love is lighter and worth more.
doha w leaf + scales: weighing learning, forgetting love
My teacher weighs every page and every leaf of paper in her marking, but cannot weigh the hurt in a student's face; a doha on that?
Late nights over study have made me like a moth circling a light, dazed and spent, while the people I love drift away.
The moth knows no pages but dies for the light; the scholar knows all pages and lives without love.
moth, reading, love
Write a doha about the scholar who, like the moth, circles round the dazzle of his learning until he is singed, never discovering that the one syllable of love is what he was seeking.
doha: moth = scholar circling endless reading w/o love
At my father's funeral, as he lay wrapped in a shroud, I realized the thousands of pages he read left no trace except a shadow of pride, while his love was what everyone mourned.
Give me a doha showing that when the shroud is drawn over the learned man, the shadow of his reading vanishes, and only the love he gave remains to be remembered by anyone.
The shroud is white and silent, the shadow of learning slips away; only love leaves a mark upon the living.
shroud, shadow, learning
doha w shroud n shadow: all that reading vanishes, love stays
doha: ppl keep going on like a spinning wheel w their reading
The spinning wheel turns all night, spinning little; the scholar reads all day, learning little of love.
My grandmother who never studied sat at her spinning wheel and understood love better than any of the scholars in our family.
I'd like a doha showing that a person may read round and round like a spinning wheel for all his life and yet remain unlettered, because the one syllable of love cannot be spun from pages.
spinning wheel, learning
doha: traveler collecting learning from every place but no love
I have been through five universities in four countries, a perpetual traveler of learning, and still I can't tell you what love is.
traveler, bookish learning
The traveler gathers pages from many lands, yet returns with empty hands, for love was never packed.
Write a doha about a traveler who wanders through many lands collecting learning in every language, yet remains unlettered because the one syllable of love can be learned only by loving.
Craft a doha about learning that is traded in the market like merchandise, bought and sold by the pound, while the single syllable of love, which no one sells, is the only learning worth having.
Everyone in my city is busy buying degrees and certificates as if at a market, but nobody is learning to be kind; doha on this?
In the market of the world learning is sold by weight, but love is a gift no one can buy.
doha: degrees sold in the market but love isnt
market, bookish learning
My cousin has read more than anyone I know but laughs at simple people for believing in kindness, and I want a doha to humble him.
Please make a doha that says the learned man who despises the humble is truly the unlettered one, because the one syllable of love is the only page that matters and he has not read it.
Though you outread the whole world, the unread heart is still a closed room.
doha: reading doesnt make u better than others
learned, unlettered
doha: our place is full of pages but no love inside, a house of study
Write a doha about a learned man whose house is stacked with volumes to the roof, yet the rooms within are cold, because he has read everything but the one syllable of love.
house, bookish learning
Our house is full of my father's volumes, and yet he never knew how to talk to us; a doha on that?
A house of pages, a heart of silence; the learned dwell among words and starve for love.
The salt dissolves into the pot, giving taste; the scholar dissolves into pages and gives none.
I need a doha showing that a scholar without love is like food without salt, full of fine material yet tasteless, because the one syllable of love is what gives all learning its flavor.
salt, learning
My teacher's lessons were thorough but bland, like a dish without salt, and I only learned to care when a kind aunt explained things simply.
doha w salt: learning without love is tasteless
I saw a lotus bloom in a muddy village pond beside a scholar muttering from his pages, and the lotus seemed to know more about beauty than he did.
lotus, bookish learning

Can you put together a doha showing that the lotus never studied a page yet blooms openly in the mud, while the scholar who has read everything remains closed, unlettered in the one syllable that matters.
doha: lotus knows love w/o reading, scholar doesnt
The lotus blooms unlettered in the mud and the scholar withers among pages; love is the only syllable it knows.
The bitter gourd grows beside the bridge of learning and stays bitter, for it never crossed into love.
bitter gourd, bridge, learning
I crossed the bridge of university into a high-paying job and remained as bitter as a bitter gourd, because I never learned kindness.
doha w bitter gourd + bridge: learning doesnt make u sweet
Write a doha showing that a bridge of learning leads nowhere if the scholar crossing it remains bitter as a bitter gourd, because the one syllable of love is the only thing that sweetens a mind.
pages without love
Give me a doha for a proud young scholar who thinks reading makes him superior, reminding him that a mother who cannot read may be more lettered in love than he will ever become.
doha on useless bookish learning
Between lines of ink the heart is never found; it is written in a language of touch and tears.
I always felt smarter than my grandmother because I could read, but she knew exactly what each of us needed without a word.
doha w mirror n cloud: scholars see themselves in pages but no love
The scholar gazes in the mirror of his learning and finds a cloud of pride; love is a clear sky he never reads.
mirror, cloud, learning
I'd like a doha showing that the mirror of the scholar's learning shows only his own face, while a cloud of pride hides the one syllable of love that would have made him truly lettered.
My friend studies to look good in front of others, like checking a mirror again and again, with a cloud over his own feelings.
doha w milk n cage: scholars caged in learning forget milk of love
milk, cage, learning
Write a doha about a scholar caged by his own reading, pouring over pages while the milk of human love goes uncollected, since the one syllable of love is learned only outside the cage.
In the cage of pages the learned are thirsty; the milk of love flows outside.
I was shut in my study cage for years chasing degrees, and missed the warm milk of family life; doha for me?
Craft a doha for scholars who argue endlessly about interpretations, saying that all the debate in the world is empty when compared with the one syllable of love that the humble learn without trying.
doha about scholars arguing but not loving
They debate the meaning of every line while the heart's one word remains unspoken.
At every family gathering my uncles debate texts and ideas for hours, and meanwhile nobody asks my grandfather how he is.
learned debaters, loveless
Please write a doha saying that the wise are not those who have read the most but those who have learned the one syllable of love, which no teacher can give and no school can examine.
I got the highest marks of my batch, and when my mother fell ill I realized I did not know how to comfort her.
lettered, not loving
doha: ppl who read a lot think theyre wise
Ink dries on pages and the heart stays dry; only love makes the reader literate.

Please make a doha showing that the washerman cleans others' garments and the moneylender counts others' coins, and the scholar reads others' pages, none of them learning the one syllable of love for himself.
The washerman scrubs, the moneylender tallies, the scholar reads; all work on others' things and none on the heart.
doha w washerman + moneylender: scholar reads for others but never learns love
washerman, moneylender, scholar
A washerman and a moneylender I know are both kinder than the learned folks in our town, and I want a doha that explains why.
Write a doha for a retiring teacher who spent his life with pages and now regrets that he never learned to say a simple word of love to his family, which was the only lesson that mattered.
doha on a learned man who regrets not loving more
learned, yet lacking love
At life's end the pages lie still, and the heart wishes it had read one syllable.
After forty years of research my father admitted he had never once told us he loved us, and I want a doha to answer that.
I want a doha reminding the clever that a mind full of other people's words is still empty of its own heart, and that the single syllable of love is the one thing no reading can supply.
My roommate quotes famous thinkers on every occasion, but when I was crying he just kept quoting; it hurt.
borrowed learning
doha: quoting ppl isnt the same as understanding
Borrowed words fill the head and leave the heart bare; only love is one's own.
The scholar draws the sword of argument against his own shadow, and wins, and is no wiser for it.
I need a doha showing that the sword of argument may win a hundred debates against the shadow of an opponent, yet the scholar remains unlettered if he has not learned the one syllable of love.
sword, shadow, learning
doha w sword n shadow: scholar wins debates but loses love
My uncle wins every argument, wielding facts like a sword, and yet he fights only shadows, because he never learned to listen with love.
